The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the top-level scope of the PKGBUILD and does not execute functions such as `pkgver()`, `build()`, `check()`, or `package()`. In this PKGBUILD, the global scope contains only standard variable assignments: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `source`, and `sha256sums`. All values are statically defined or constructed from trusted, deterministic expressions using the package's own version and name. The `source` array refers to versioned release artifacts from the project's official GitHub repository and uses pinned checksums. There are no command substitutions, function calls, or executable statements at the top level that would trigger network activity, file system modifications, or data exfiltration when sourcing the file. Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>

The build process uses standard autotools workflow (configure, make) and installs binaries, headers, and shared libraries to appropriate system directories.

The license is properly declared and installed.

The use of `mkdir -p build` and out-of-source build via a subdirectory is a common and safe practice. The shared library installation includes proper SONAME handling via a symlink. All steps align with standard Arch Linux packaging guidelines and the expected behavior of a C-based database tool with version control features.
</details>
